subject: Data placement constraints & failback plan for BrightWell POC
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@brightwellhealth.com>
Cc: Elaine Chen <elaine.chen@brightwellhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Data placement constraints & failback plan for BrightWell POC

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet you both. Below is a short recap of the data handling and residency requirements we captured, plus proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. Please correct me where I mis-summarize.

Summary of requirements (as discussed)
- EU patient data must remain in EU datacenters for both live inference and backups unless explicit legal approval is provided by BrightWell legal.
- US patient data must remain in US datacenters; multi-region access for analytics is not allowed unless data is pseudonymized.
- Audit logs (access/change) required for at least 24 months; ability to export filtered logs within 48 hours for audits.
- Backups: encrypted at rest with customer KMS preferred (BYOK). Default retention: 90 days for full snapshots; longer retention for legal holds (per-case).
- DR: BrightWell requires a documented failback plan and approval for cross-region replication. If cross-region replication is required for RTO/RPO, copies must remain encrypted with CMK and access-limited; metadata indicating origin region must be preserved.

How Redwood can meet these needs (high-level)
- Region pinning: our serving layer supports per-tenant/model region pinning — requests are routed to instances in the pinned region.
- Storage/backup: by default backups are stored in the same region as the primary; we support encrypted snapshot export to an authenticated DR region when customer contract permits.
- Key management: we support customer-managed keys (KMS) for both runtime encryption and backup encryption; we can rotate keys per-tenant.
- Audit logs: per-tenant access logs collected and retained; we can configure retention policies and provide exports for compliance.

Open questions / items for BrightWell to confirm
1) For the POC, do you want backups strictly restricted to-region (no DR copies) or are you comfortable with encrypted cross-region replication to a specific DR region with contractual guardrails?
2) Which datasets are considered PII that must never cross borders? (names, SSNs, PHI? — please share the attachments you referred to on the call)
3) Any preferred SLA targets for RPO/RTO for the POC?

Attachments: redwood-region-pin-guide.pdf (short tech overview), SOC2-Type2-2026.pdf (Redwood attestation)

Proposed next steps
- I’ll follow up with our security lead (Grace) to assemble a limited-scope evidence packet and a draft failback playbook.
- If agreeable, schedule a 30-45 minute technical walkthrough next week to go over architecture and approval workflow.

Thanks — Neha

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@brightwellhealth.com>

Date: 2026-11-22T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data placement constraints & failback plan for BrightWell POC

Hi Neha — thanks, that summary is helpful. A couple clarifying questions from our infra/legal teams: 

1) Nightly backups: are these kept in the same region by default or do you already replicate them to a hot DR region? BrightWell policy currently requires EU backups to remain in EU unless we explicitly sign off on DR replication.
2) If we allow cross-region replication for DR, can we limit it to encrypted snapshots only (no live read access in DR region) and ensure that the snapshot metadata keeps a clear origin-region flag?
3) RPO/RTO: our initial ask for the POC is RPO <= 1 hour and RTO <= 4 hours but we need to understand any additional costs for hitting those targets.

I attached a quick spreadsheet with the datasets we consider regulated (BrightWell-data-requirements.xlsx). Can Grace or your security team confirm that the SOC2 evidence + region-pin guide will be enough for our compliance review, or do you expect more artifacts?

Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Cloud Ops | BrightWell Health
sanjay.patel@brightwellhealth.com | +1 (650) 555-0987

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Data placement constraints & failback plan for BrightWell POC

Looping Grace for security details — quick notes / suggested answers to Sanjay’s questions: 

- Nightly backups: default behavior is in-region only. We can enable an encrypted export flow to an agreed DR region; exports are immutable snapshots encrypted with CMK. For strict EU-only requirements, recommend Private or Dedicated with contractual restrictions (we can disable cross-region export at the tenant level).
- Snapshot metadata: we do preserve origin-region metadata in the snapshot object and in S3-style manifests; we can add a policy that prevents automated restore outside origin region without an explicit signed approval workflow.
- RPO/RTO: 1h/4h is achievable on Dedicated with our standard snapshot+replicate configuration. On Hosted there are tradeoffs; hitting RPO=1h will require more frequent incremental snapshotting and/or a small warm standby in DR which has cost implications. We should prepare an options matrix with estimated incremental monthly costs for: hosted-no-DR, hosted-with-DR-export, dedicated-with-warm-standby, private-on-prem.

Grace — can you prepare:
1) A short evidence checklist (SOC2 sections, KMS configuration notes, audit-log export steps) we can send to BrightWell legal.
2) A short failback playbook draft (1-2 pages) that shows restore steps, approvals required, and region re-pin workflow.

Neha — I’ll draft the options matrix and finish the incremental cost bullets for the call.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@brightwellhealth.com>, Elaine Chen <elaine.chen@brightwellhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Data placement constraints & failback plan for BrightWell POC

Hi Sanjay / Elaine — appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Nightly backups: default is region-local. For the POC we can keep backups strictly in-region by configuration; cross-region replication will only be enabled if BrightWell signs off and we add the export clause to the MSA.
- Cross-region replication: supported as encrypted snapshot export only; no live read access in DR unless you approve a warm-standby option. Snapshot manifests will include origin-region flags and we can add an approval gate in the restore workflow.
- RPO/RTO: we can meet RPO <=1h and RTO <=4h on Dedicated or Private. For Hosted we can aim for 1h RPO with extra incremental snapshot frequency but there will be additional cost — Marcus will provide numbers in the options matrix.

Next steps I propose:
1) Grace will attach the evidence checklist and a one-page draft failback playbook (see draft_fallback_playbook.md).
2) Marcus will share an options matrix with incremental monthly costs for the DR configurations.
3) Schedule a 30–45 minute technical call to walk BrightWell infra/legal through the artifacts and confirm dataset classification. How does Friday 2026-11-26 at 10:00 AM PT look for your team?

I’ll upload the two artifacts to the shared drive and send the link when ready.

Thanks — Neha
